adjusts.description: Hat state PV; 0 drives the configured pins LOW and any other value drives them HIGH (the IOC stores the resulting HIGH/LOW level)
adjusts.name: hat_state

device.name: Raspberry Pi hat IOC (caproto EPICS Channel Access)

facts.text: iocs/hat.py defines IOC with a state pvproperty (default 0) whose put callback is write_state; write_state maps a truthy value to GPIO.HIGH and a falsy value to GPIO.LOW and writes that level to every configured pin.
The state startup hook selects GPIO.BOARD numbering, configures every pin as an output and drives it LOW; the shutdown hook drives every pin LOW and calls GPIO.cleanup.
The hat IOC requires a comma-separated --pins argument, converts each token to int and passes the list to IOC(pins=...).
The hat IOC argument parser sets default_prefix='rpi:'.
The hats.yml playbook copies only hat.py into /opt/iocs.

iocs/rgb.py defines IOC with a color pvproperty whose default value is the one-element list ['000000']; write_color parses value[0] as a base-16 integer, sets every channel duty cycle and returns value.
rescale maps an 8-bit channel value to 100 * (x / 255)**2.8, a 0-100 duty-cycle scale with gamma 2.8; the comment attributes 2.8 to the RGB LED vendor.
duty_cycle extracts the red, green and blue 8-bit channels with the masks 0xff0000, 0x00ff00 and 0x0000ff and rescales each.
The color startup hook selects GPIO.BOARD numbering, configures each channel pin as an output LOW, creates one 2000 Hz PWM object per channel and starts each at duty 0.
The color shutdown hook sets every PWM channel to duty 0, stops it, drives every pin LOW and calls GPIO.cleanup.
The rgb IOC argument parser sets default_prefix='rpi:'.
The rgb IOC requires --red, --green and --blue BOARD pin arguments and passes them to IOC(red=..., green=..., blue=...).

operator_required.name: hat_state
operator_required.reason: the IOC maps any truthy value to GPIO.HIGH and any falsy value to GPIO.LOW; no line states a numeric input range for the state PV

safe_state.description: Hat state PV written 0 and read back 0: write_state drove every configured hat pin LOW (proven only as the IOC's executed put, not as a sensed pin level). The stop does not run GPIO.cleanup; the rgb IOC and anything else on the Pi are outside it.
